name: ShadowKV: KV Cache in Shadows for High-Throughput Long-Context LLM Inference
problem: Dynamic sparse attention either does not cut GPU memory enough, or gets large decode latency by offloading the KV cache to CPU memory.
mechanism: Split the KV cache by ASYMMETRY rather than recency: keep a LOW-RANK key cache resident on the GPU and offload the VALUE cache to CPU. Then, instead of streaming values back, reconstruct MINIMAL SPARSE KV pairs on the fly - select which tokens matter, reconstruct their keys from the low-rank GPU-resident representation, and fetch only those values. The selection strategy is accurate specifically so that the reconstruction error does not show up in the output.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claim (abstract): on RULER, LongBench and Needle-In-A-Haystack with Llama-3.1-8B, Llama-3-8B-1M, GLM-4-9B-1M, Yi-9B-200K, Phi-3-Mini-128K and Qwen2-7B-128K, supports up to 6x LARGER BATCH SIZES and boosts throughput by up to 3.04x ON AN A100 GPU, without sacrificing accuracy. COMPRESSION RATIO: low-rank key cache + CPU-offloaded value cache (not a bit-width scheme). QUALITY COST: 'without sacrificing accuracy' per the abstract - the batch-size increase (6x) is the more useful operating point than the throughput number.
